doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Money and living arrangements in the Sun Ra band
summary: Griffin describes band members pooling gig money for rent, Sun Ra's cash and money belt, and the band acting as bodyguards.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Were those fellows making any — hmm — were they making any money working with Sun Ra or was it more like this is just something I really need to do?

Well they were making money. Let me see, now John Gilmore, he had a choice. Well he did, he played with Mingus, he played with Art Blakey. He recorded with Art Blakey. And he could have gone and been out there and played in the band but the music that Sun Ra was writing and creating was so challenging. That’s what kept him into Sun Ra’s music. He would mention, he said, Monk had some really hip and but he said he was more interested in what Sun Ra was doing harmonically in those intervals. And the reason, I don’t know why but they kind of like decided that they loved music so all they wanted to do was play music and have a place to live and everything. And Sun Ra at the time I used to go — Sun Ra rehearsed every day all day. Every day all day. And I lived in New York and I was married and did — I was teaching and my son was just born and everything. But the guys who lived in the house with Sun Ra, and they pooled — I’m pretty sure they pooled their money, you know, for some basic stuff like Sun Ra would — would pay the rent. It was a joint effort and whatever gig they got, you know, they got

paid and then whatever portion of their rent, you know, went in. So I never truly understand it. But one thing I did know and I can say, Sun Ra never had a bank account so he dealt — most of his money was in cash — ten thousand — I remember going to Europe and Sun Ra would have these kind of dashiki things he had made these clothes, and he had a money belt. And I used to see that and I’ve seen his money belt. And he would have all of his money on him or somewhere, and then he always had members of the band around him and they were like his bodyguards. I figured that one out. I took it to the extent — and every time we went out someplace, you know, Sun Ra was never hardly alone because of I guess that. He always had the band around him and those guys were really really very quick in martial arts and everything. No weapons or anything but they could take care.
